about: The square below the balcony as the game draws it beyond its kit: the harbour, the far ground, the launch view (its own stage), the square's lamps, the floodlights from the towers, the stage lamp, the moonlight and the night sky. Frame: EarthSite's own.

stars.from: game/world/sky/sky.gd:19-33,517-544 (SEED 9, STAR_COUNT 1800, SKY_DISTANCE 700: a SphereMesh of radius 0.7 with 4 sides and 2 rings, scaled 0.4 to 1.3, every direction), game/art/materials/star.tres (unshaded #eef2ff); hung here at 1900 m with each star as wide seen from the middle, past everything the stage holds and inside the views' 2000 m reach, as the game hangs them just inside its camera's reach; turned with the place's own axes, where the game turns them with the world's spin and the hour, which the record does not carry

game_only: the far city across the harbour is the framework's own, in 3D (the far_city place, tools/usd/far_city_stage.py, seed 7): 2,188 made towers of five kinds rows deep along a far shore 1.3 to 1.8 km off, their windows lit, with code-built mountains behind and water out to the shore; the pencil tower, the low waterfront block and the housing slab are not made yet, so their lots carry the made kinds and the waterfront has no low blocks. The game hangs four photographs of Hong Kong there instead (earth_site.gd:327-335,959-972), which no stage carries
the crowd's look up close: the game's people are flat-shaded and lit by the stage, the scene's are its own skinned characters
the lit columns the game paints onto the water (each lit thing's streak, harbour.gdshader's lit_columns); the water mirrors what stands round it
the stars' turn: the field is the game's own (its seed, count and sizes), turned with the place's axes, not with the world's spin and the hour
owner_rejected: the night market's stalls and the stage's screens: the game draws both, and the owner rejected them for the scene (2026-10-09)
